surfaceForm: the proportion of remote versus on-campus subjects ... a single physical campus is presupposed throughout the sizing narrative ("on-campus subjects")
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Method and assumptions} (\S sec:sz-method, "Sources of variation")
proposedGenericDecision: Frame the on-/off-premises split as a generic estate-topology variable (sites/locations) rather than presupposing one campus; let the role be 'the institution's physical estate' of arbitrary cardinality.
rationale: "on-campus" silently assumes a single-campus institution; an institution-agnostic document should phrase this as on-premises vs remote across the institution's site(s), since multi-campus is later acknowledged only as an exception.

surfaceForm: that the single-site reference does not address ... the single-site reference
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Scaling levers and breakpoints} (\S sec:sz-scaling, "Multi-site institutions" bullet)
proposedGenericDecision: Make site cardinality an explicit parameter of the reference profile rather than hard-coding the reference as single-site; the agnostic baseline should state how many sites the reference assumes and treat multi-site as a configuration, not an afterthought.
rationale: The whole breakpoint section is anchored on an implicit single physical site / single data-centre, which is an institution-specific topology assumption. The reference institution (University of Luxembourg) is effectively single-site; a portable doc must not bake that in.

surfaceForm: engineer-equivalents per layer (2--4, 1--2, 3--5, 4--7, 2--4, 3--6, 3--5, 1--2, 2--4) and "an additional one to two engineer-equivalents per active wave"
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{FTE indicators per layer} (\S sec:sz-fte, Table tab:sz-fte and "Build versus run split")
proposedGenericDecision: FTE envelopes are labour-market / jurisdiction bound; keep them as role-based effort ranges but flag that the headcount-to-effort mapping is jurisdiction-dependent, or parameterize the staffing assumptions behind the numbers.
rationale: FTE figures implicitly assume a particular labour market, role structure and skill availability. They are presented as indicative ranges tied to the reference instantiation, so they can stay, but they carry an unstated jurisdiction/cost assumption worth flagging.

surfaceForm: single-cluster Keycloak deployment of the reference
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Scaling levers and breakpoints} (\S sec:sz-scaling, "Identity above ~50k subjects")
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the identity-provider role (the reference identity cluster) rather than the specific product; product names belong to the reference instantiation, not the institution-agnostic architecture layer.
rationale: Keycloak is a concrete product chosen for the reference instantiation. It is not UL-named per se, but it is a deployment-specific instantiation choice that prevents the breakpoint from being product-agnostic; the breakpoint (partitioning above a scale) is the portable content.

surfaceForm: single-cluster OpenSearch deployment of the reference ... a per-GB priced alternative
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Scaling levers and breakpoints} (\S sec:sz-scaling, "Audit above ~500 GB/day")
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the audit/analytical-store role and to tiering; keep the per-GB-pricing caution as a generic cost-model caveat without binding it to the reference product.
rationale: OpenSearch is a reference-instantiation product choice; the architectural lesson (data-tier separation, watch per-GB-priced stores) is generic and should be expressed against the analytical-store role.

surfaceForm: single-instance OPA deployment of the reference
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Scaling levers and breakpoints} (\S sec:sz-scaling, "Policy above ~5000 decisions/s")
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the policy-decision-point role; sidecar-per-application with centrally coordinated bundle distribution is the portable pattern, independent of OPA.
rationale: OPA is a specific policy-engine product of the reference instantiation. The breakpoint and the sidecar pattern are product-agnostic.

surfaceForm: single-cluster Ceph deployment of the reference ... federation across multiple Ceph clusters ... Ceph operations require dedicated familiarity
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \S sec:sz-scaling ("Storage above multi-petabyte") and Table tab:sz-fte (Storage Ch.10 note)
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the object/block-storage role (the reference storage cluster); cluster-federation-with-metadata-coordination is the generic lever above the multi-petabyte breakpoint.
rationale: Ceph appears twice as the reference storage product. The breakpoint and the federation lever are product-independent; the product name is an instantiation detail.

surfaceForm: Sustained engineering investment for OpenStack + Kubernetes
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{FTE indicators per layer} (Table tab:sz-fte, Compute Ch.9 note)
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the virtualisation + container-orchestration roles rather than the specific products of the reference stack.
rationale: OpenStack and Kubernetes name the reference instantiation's compute stack; the FTE point (sustained investment for the IaaS + orchestration combination) holds for any equivalent stack.

surfaceForm: these can be drawn from a national research cloud, an \gls{nren}-provided service, or a managed provider under an appropriate data-processing agreement
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Down-scaled profile...} (\S sec:sz-downscale, "Managed or mutualised compute and storage")
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the role-based options (national/sector research cloud, NREN service, managed provider) generic; the "national" qualifier already abstracts the specific country, so retain but ensure no single country's offering is presumed available.
rationale: This is an implicit national-provision assumption (a national research cloud / NREN service is presumed to exist for the institution) stated without naming the country. It is already role-based and country-neutral, but it assumes such national infrastructure is available; flag/parameterize for jurisdictions where it is not.

surfaceForm: a research-cloud presence in multiple jurisdictions face additional design decisions (... cross-site policy consistency ...)
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Scaling levers and breakpoints} (\S sec:sz-scaling, "Multi-site institutions")
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as a generic multi-jurisdiction caveat; ensure it reads as applicable to any institution operating across borders, not as a Luxembourg/EU-specific framing.
rationale: Mentions cross-jurisdiction research-cloud presence without naming jurisdictions; already country-neutral, low risk, included for completeness of the jurisdiction-bound sweep.

surfaceForm: cold-tier (object storage, retrievable) for the period required by regulatory and audit obligations, typically several years
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Audit and observability layer sizing} (\S sec:sz-audit, retention scenario)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the retention as a generic 'period required by applicable regulatory and audit obligations'; the specific years are a local-law parameter and are already left to the institution.
rationale: Retention duration is jurisdiction-bound (local regulatory obligations); the text already abstracts it to 'as required by obligations', so it is portable, but the implicit assumption that such obligations dictate the period is jurisdiction-dependent and worth parameterizing.

surfaceForm: ~25k active subjects, ~1.5k staff with elevated access, ~500 active research projects; research-intensive (R1) university
location: ch15-sizing-EN.tex, \section{Method and assumptions} (\S sec:sz-method, "Reference profile"); also header comment D15.1
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the reference profile as an explicitly-labelled indicative scale anchor, but expose its three magnitudes as named profile parameters so an adopting institution substitutes its own scale rather than inheriting the reference one.
rationale: The 25k/1.5k/500 R1 profile mirrors the source institution's scale. It is explicitly framed as indicative and methodological (not a measurement), so it can stay, but the magnitudes are an institution-shaped anchor that should be parameterizable for portability.

surfaceForm: eduGAIN, SCIM, NAC, IPFIX, Science DMZ, perfSONAR(implied), federation
proposedGenericDecision: Retain: these are open standards / vendor-neutral architectural concepts, not institution-specific. No genericisation needed.
rationale: eduGAIN/SCIM/NAC/IPFIX/Science DMZ are sector-standard, vendor- and institution-neutral terms; included explicitly to record that they were reviewed and judged portable as-is.
